quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in vs on vs at
quests.spatialHierarchy: Enclosed Space / Volume (e.g. in the room)
quests.question: You can see the Eiffel Tower ___ the background of this picture.
quests.targetSentence: You can see the Eiffel Tower in the background of this picture.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in vs on vs at
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In the background' is a fixed phrase treating a photo's depth as an enclosed space, the same logic used for rooms or containers.
quests.nativeTip: A photograph has depth, and this spot is enclosed within that visual space.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in' (Enclosed Space / Volume (e.g. in the room)) ➔ 'You can see the Eiffel Tower in the background of this picture.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in vs on vs at
quests.question: We first met ___ a mutual friend's wedding.
quests.targetSentence: We first met at a mutual friend's wedding.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in vs on vs at
quests.ruleExplanation: 'At' is used for events treated as a point in space and time, like a wedding; 'during' would instead describe something happening within a stretch of time.
quests.nativeTip: This treats the event itself as the point of reference, not a period of time.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'at' (Specific Point (e.g. at the door)) ➔ 'We first met at a mutual friend's wedding.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in vs on vs at
quests.question: The instructions are printed ___ the back of the box.
quests.targetSentence: The instructions are printed on the back of the box.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: in vs on vs at
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On' fits printed text resting on a surface, completing the three-way contrast alongside 'in' and 'at'.
quests.nativeTip: Printed text sits on a flat surface, not inside a hollow space.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on' (Surface Contact (e.g. on the table)) ➔ 'The instructions are printed on the back of the box.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: between vs among
quests.question: The rivalry ___ the two brothers went back decades.
quests.targetSentence: The rivalry between the two brothers went back decades.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Between' is used for exactly two people or things; 'among' would be used for three or more.
quests.nativeTip: Exactly two people are named here.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'between' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The rivalry between the two brothers went back decades.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: between vs among
quests.question: She felt completely at ease ___ strangers at the party.
quests.targetSentence: She felt completely at ease among strangers at the party.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Among' fits an unspecified group of three or more, unlike 'between', which is reserved for exactly two.
quests.nativeTip: This describes being surrounded by an unspecified group, not just two people.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'among' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She felt completely at ease among strangers at the party.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: between vs among
quests.question: The prize will be divided ___ the top three winners.
quests.targetSentence: The prize will be divided among the top three winners.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Among' is correct because the prize is shared by three winners, the same group-size rule taught earlier in this level.
quests.nativeTip: Three people share this, following the same rule as the party example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'among' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The prize will be divided among the top three winners.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: above vs over
quests.question: The mountain village sits ___ the clouds, invisible from the valley below.
quests.targetSentence: The mountain village sits above the clouds, invisible from the valley below.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Above' describes a general higher position without implying direct contact or motion; 'over' more often suggests being directly overhead or in motion across something.
quests.nativeTip: This is about a fixed, general higher position, not something passing directly overhead.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'above' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The mountain village sits above the clouds, invisible from the valley below.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: above vs over
quests.question: The old oak tree's branches spread ___ the entire garden, casting shade on everything below.
quests.targetSentence: The old oak tree's branches spread over the entire garden, casting shade on everything below.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Over' fits because the branches cover the garden from above, creating shade — 'across' would only describe spreading sideways, without that sense of coverage.
quests.nativeTip: Something is covering the space from directly overhead, which the mention of shade confirms.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'over' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The old oak tree's branches spread over the entire garden, casting shade on everything below.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: above vs over
quests.question: The concert attracted ___ ten thousand fans from across the country.
quests.targetSentence: The concert attracted over ten thousand fans from across the country.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Over' is the common way to express 'more than' with a number, such as a crowd size.
quests.nativeTip: This word is the standard choice for describing a quantity greater than a stated number.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'over' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The concert attracted over ten thousand fans from across the country.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: below vs under
quests.question: The cat is hiding ___ the bed, refusing to come out.
quests.targetSentence: The cat is hiding under the bed, refusing to come out.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Under' fits direct physical positions beneath something concrete, like furniture; 'below' is more common for abstract levels or measurements.
quests.nativeTip: This is a direct physical position beneath a concrete object.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'under' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The cat is hiding under the bed, refusing to come out.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: below vs under
quests.question: Temperatures are expected to drop ___ freezing tonight.
quests.targetSentence: Temperatures are expected to drop below freezing tonight.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Below' is the standard choice for measurements and thresholds, such as temperature, rather than physical position.
quests.nativeTip: This is the standard word for describing a measurement falling under a threshold.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'below' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Temperatures are expected to drop below freezing tonight.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: below vs under
quests.question: Keep the spare key ___ the doormat, just in case you're locked out.
quests.targetSentence: Keep the spare key under the doormat, just in case you're locked out.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Under' fits again here, describing a physical object placed directly beneath something else, the same pattern as the earlier example.
quests.nativeTip: This is a concrete object placed directly beneath another one, just like the cat example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'under' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Keep the spare key under the doormat, just in case you're locked out.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: beside vs besides
quests.question: He sat quietly ___ his grandmother during the long service.
quests.targetSentence: He sat quietly beside his grandmother during the long service.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Beside' describes physical position next to someone, unlike 'besides', which means 'in addition to'.
quests.nativeTip: This describes physical closeness, not an additional idea.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'beside' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He sat quietly beside his grandmother during the long service.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: beside vs besides
quests.question: What else should I order, ___ the salad?
quests.targetSentence: What else should I order, besides the salad?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Besides' means 'in addition to' when introducing another item; 'apart' alone is incomplete without 'from', and 'beside' would only describe physical location.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces an additional item, not a spatial position.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'besides' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'What else should I order, besides the salad?'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: beside vs besides
quests.question: She's an amazing host, ___ being a fantastic cook.
quests.targetSentence: She's an amazing host, besides being a fantastic cook.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Besides' introduces an additional quality here, just like it introduced an additional menu item earlier in this level.
quests.nativeTip: This adds an extra quality, following the same pattern as the earlier menu example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'besides' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She's an amazing host, besides being a fantastic cook.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs with
quests.question: We traveled ___ train instead of flying, to see more of the countryside.
quests.targetSentence: We traveled by train instead of flying, to see more of the countryside.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'By' is used for a method of transport in the fixed pattern 'by + [mode of transport]', without an article before the noun.
quests.nativeTip: This names a method of transport, used without an article before the noun.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'by' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We traveled by train instead of flying, to see more of the countryside.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs with
quests.question: She fixed the leaky faucet ___ just a wrench and some tape.
quests.targetSentence: She fixed the leaky faucet with just a wrench and some tape.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'With' introduces the tool or instrument used to carry out an action, unlike 'by', which more often introduces a method or an agent.
quests.nativeTip: This links an action to the physical tools used to perform it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'with' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She fixed the leaky faucet with just a wrench and some tape.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs with
quests.question: The novel was written ___ a first-time author who later won several awards.
quests.targetSentence: The novel was written by a first-time author who later won several awards.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'By' introduces the agent — the person who performed the action — in a passive-voice sentence.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces who performed the action in a passive sentence.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'by' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The novel was written by a first-time author who later won several awards.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: from vs of
quests.question: This cheese comes ___ a small farm in the Swiss Alps.
quests.targetSentence: This cheese comes from a small farm in the Swiss Alps.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Comes from' names the origin or source of something, such as a farm.
quests.nativeTip: This names the place something originated from.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'This cheese comes from a small farm in the Swiss Alps.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: from vs of
quests.question: The necklace is made ___ pure silver.
quests.targetSentence: The necklace is made of pure silver.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Made of' is used when the original material stays recognizable in the finished item, like silver in a necklace; 'made from' fits materials that are transformed, like grapes into wine.
quests.nativeTip: The original material is still clearly recognizable in the final product.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The necklace is made of pure silver.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: from vs of
quests.question: This paper is made ___ recycled wood pulp, which is then processed and pressed.
quests.targetSentence: This paper is made from recycled wood pulp, which is then processed and pressed.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Made from' fits here because wood pulp is processed and pressed into something quite different, contrasting with the silver necklace example.
quests.nativeTip: The original material is heavily transformed before it becomes the final product.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'This paper is made from recycled wood pulp, which is then processed and pressed.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: to vs for
quests.question: Please give this letter ___ your supervisor as soon as possible.
quests.targetSentence: Please give this letter to your supervisor as soon as possible.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To' introduces the direct recipient of an action, such as handing over a letter.
quests.nativeTip: This names the person directly receiving the object being handed over.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Please give this letter to your supervisor as soon as possible.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: to vs for
quests.question: I bought this gift ___ my sister's birthday next week.
quests.targetSentence: I bought this gift for my sister's birthday next week.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'For' introduces the purpose, benefit, or occasion behind an action, such as a birthday.
quests.nativeTip: This links the gift to its purpose or occasion, not a direct recipient action.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'for' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'I bought this gift for my sister's birthday next week.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: to vs for
quests.question: She made a delicious cake ___ the office party, and everyone loved it.
quests.targetSentence: She made a delicious cake for the office party, and everyone loved it.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'For' fits again here, showing the purpose behind making the cake, the same logic as the birthday gift example.
quests.nativeTip: This links the cake to the occasion it was made for, matching the earlier gift example.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'for' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She made a delicious cake for the office party, and everyone loved it.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: across vs through
quests.question: A shadow moved quickly ___ the field as the clouds passed overhead.
quests.targetSentence: A shadow moved quickly across the field as the clouds passed overhead.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Across' fits movement over an open, flat area like a field.
quests.nativeTip: This is movement over a flat, open area, not through an enclosed space.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'across' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'A shadow moved quickly across the field as the clouds passed overhead.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: across vs through
quests.question: It took hours to drive ___ the dense traffic downtown.
quests.targetSentence: It took hours to drive through the dense traffic downtown.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Through' fits movement within something that surrounds you, like heavy traffic, contrasting with the open-field example.
quests.nativeTip: Traffic surrounds a car on all sides, unlike an open field.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'through' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'It took hours to drive through the dense traffic downtown.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: around vs about
quests.question: This documentary is ___ the history of jazz music.
quests.targetSentence: This documentary is about the history of jazz music.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'About' introduces a topic or subject matter, distinct from 'around', which is mainly used for physical movement or approximate numbers.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces the subject or topic of something, not a physical movement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'about' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'This documentary is about the history of jazz music.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: by vs until
quests.question: The negotiations lasted ___ midnight, well past what anyone expected.
quests.targetSentence: The negotiations lasted until midnight, well past what anyone expected.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Until' shows the negotiations continued right up to midnight, longer than expected — 'by' would instead suggest they were finished at or before that point.
quests.nativeTip: The talks kept going right up to that hour, rather than finishing earlier.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'until' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The negotiations lasted until midnight, well past what anyone expected.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: since vs for
quests.question: The company's revenue has grown steadily ___ the merger two years ago.
quests.targetSentence: The company's revenue has grown steadily since the merger two years ago.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of an ongoing change, here the merger two years ago.
quests.nativeTip: A specific past event marks the starting point of this ongoing trend.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'since' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The company's revenue has grown steadily since the merger two years ago.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Dependent Prepositions: Nouns
quests.question: He succeeded in convincing the board despite fierce opposition ___ several senior members.
quests.targetSentence: He succeeded in convincing the board despite fierce opposition from several senior members.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Opposition from' names the source of resistance — the senior members who opposed him.
quests.nativeTip: This links the opposition to the people it came from.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He succeeded in convincing the board despite fierce opposition from several senior members.'
